body.heading: How the rhythm goes
paragraphs: The best-known version, the Pomodoro Technique, uses twenty-five minutes of focused work followed by a five-minute break, with a longer break after four rounds. The numbers are not magic; the rhythm is the point.
Knowing a break is coming makes it easier to park distractions: write the stray thought on paper and return to it in the break, rather than chasing it now.

body.heading: Adjust it to your task
paragraphs: Some work wants longer stretches: writing or coding may settle better at forty or fifty minutes. Some days only manage fifteen. Experiment and keep the version you actually use.
Protect the breaks as fiercely as the focus. Stand up, look at something far away, get water. A break spent scrolling is a poor trade, and you will feel the difference by the third round.

takeaway: Focus in timed rounds with real breaks, and tune the lengths to your work.
